newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel CPI-linked bonds higher on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Israel CPI-linked bonds higher on tight supply.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher across the board on Monday with prices of CPI-linked bonds leading the gains on fears of tight supply in August, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.3 pct to 111.12
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.37 pct to 111.37
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.12 pct to 110.23
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.12 pct to 110.95
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 108.47
Volume including Makams was a low 134 million shekels.
"CPI-linked bonds rose today because of fears of a tight supply of these bonds in August," said Tiki Haddad of IBI Investment House.

"Government bond redemptions are expected to total four billion shekels in August against issues of 1.6 billion shekels," Haddad said. "Also, the news of a rise in government tax revenues will cause the government to raise less debt," she said.
Traders said that the shortage was expected to affect all government bonds but especially CPI-linked bonds.
The Treasury said on Monday that Israel's tax revenues since the beginning of the year totalled 62.8 billion shekels, a real increase of 1.3 percent from 55 billion a year earlier.
"Prices of CPI-linked bonds rose today because the central bank did not issue any new CPI-linked bonds this week," said Gila Shkury, an investment manager at Israel Discount Bank.
"Trading volume was low today, which indicates that people who have bonds are not selling them."
She added that fears of rising inflation in coming months were also pushing up demand for CPI-linked bonds.

The advance of the dollar against the shekel in June, which caused June's CPI to rise a steep 1.1 percent, has triggered fears of a series of high indices in July and August. The shekel has recovered some of its losses against the dollar in the past two weeks.
Prices of unlinked bonds rose on Monday because money funds purchase their bonds at the beginning of each month, Haddad said, and because yields of these bonds were relatively high.
Yields of one-year unlinked bonds were around 13 percent.

Prices of dollar-linked bonds rose due to the gains in the the dollar against the shekel, Shkury said. The shekel weakened slightly against the dollar on Monday. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5410 shekels compared with 3.5370 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.54 shekels)
